alice: heads-up — after rolling the python-sdk 3.2.1 build into our staging fleet we saw steady file descriptor growth during the burst load test, sockets piling up and eventually hitting ulimits :grimacing:
ben: ouch. any logs or a repro?
alice: pasted a trimmed netstat/snippet from the runner:
```
tcp        0      0 10.0.0.5:56012        34.120.100.2:443        ESTABLISHED  -
tcp        0      0 10.0.0.5:56013        34.120.100.2:443        TIME_WAIT    -
... (100s of 10.0.0.5:56xxx -> 34.120.100.2:443)
```
and our test harness shows fd count per worker climbing: 120 -> 520 -> 980 over ~15m.
carla: are you creating an AsyncClient inside the request handler by any chance? that's a classic leak if you don't close it.
alice: here's the minimal handler we use in the load-test harness (reduced):
```
async def handle(req):
    client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
    res = await client.chat.create(model="rwd/fast", messages=req.messages)
    return res
```
ben: yep — creating per-call without closing. normally that works because AsyncClient finalizer closes transport, but in 3.2.1 we changed keep-alive/transport layering (attempt to improve perf) and finalizer timing on some pythons no longer triggers promptly. result: sockets stick around until process exit.
sasha: workaround for now: reuse a single AsyncClient across workers or explicitly use `async with AsyncClient(...)` in your handler. also you can set env REDWOOD_MAX_CONNECTIONS=50 to limit growth while we patch.
carla: can we add a guard in the SDK to detect per-request client creation? maybe a runtime warning when >X clients created in Y seconds. would help DX.
ben: good idea. I'll open an issue and a quick PR. plan: (1) make transport closing explicit in AsyncClient.__del__ and add a weakref-finalizer fallback, (2) add docs + FAQ about reusing client instances, (3) add telemetry to detect excessive client churn.
alice: awesome. can you tag this as a regression? our perf runs were stable on 3.2.0 and started regressing on 3.2.1.
ben: will do — issue #1234 created and assigned. starting a PR now.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback initiated for python-sdk 3.2.1 -> 3.2.0 in staging canary at 2025-10-03T12:34:00Z :white_check_mark:
sasha: i'll add a short load test that creates the bad pattern and assert fd stays < 200 after 10m. putting it in CI as an integration check.
ben: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/1278 — fixes finalizer and adds doc blurb. will request backport to v3.2.x.
carla: also add a tiny snippet in quickstart showing long-lived client usage, e.g.:
```
# module scope
client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)

async def handler(req):
    return await client.chat.create(...)
```
alice: confirmed that switching tests to a global client stops fd growth. thanks everyone :pray:
ben: no problem — will post updates in this thread when PR lands and backport is cut.
sasha: marking follow-up: add CI integr test + docs.
alice: closing loop here once backport is available. thanks :rocket:
